name: A blank value is not greater, not less, and not equal to anything except another blank
why: This is the rule that decides whether a guard fires on a record somebody has not filled in yet, and it is the one every naive implementation gets wrong. Treating a missing number as zero makes `amount lt 100` true for every unfilled record, and a workflow built on it fires on rows nobody has touched.

cases.why: Both false, and deliberately. `lt` and `gt` are not each other's negation once a blank is involved.
An empty string is blank. A text field cleared in a form arrives as "", not as null.
So is an empty list. A multiselect with nothing chosen is not the same as one nobody has looked at, but for a guard it is.
A field the record does not have at all reads as blank rather than throwing.
Two blanks are equal. `neq` against a blank is therefore false, which is what makes "changed to something" expressible.

A blank is not in the list, so notIn is TRUE for a record nobody has filled in. Debatable, and settled here: `in` and `notIn` are exact negations of each other, which is the property somebody writing a pair of workflows depends on.
